recKdub4aNd78D98d.Bio: David Warner Mathisen is a prolific author of astrotheology and "star myth" research, arguing that world mythologies and scriptures share a common ancient celestial symbolic system; he has appeared on InnerVerse multiple times (Star Myths, Ophiuchus, Thor, Aboriginal astronomy).
recKdub4aNd78D98d.Name: David Warner Mathisen

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Serpent Bearer Left Out of the Zodiac", "body": "David Warner Mathisen argues that Ophiuchus is the pivotal but suppressed figure of the ancient star myth system. The sun genuinely crosses its foot each December, yet the constellation is excluded from the twelve signs, making it a perfect liminal or threshold figure with one foot in and one foot out. Mathisen traces the same serpent bearer through Jesus, Krishna, Buddha, Solomon, Moses, Athena, Asclepius and even Loki, and Chance Garton opens by noting that InnerVerse itself was born under this asterism back in 2015."}, {"title": "Mario Garza and the Argument for the Pole", "body": "Mario Garza brings a northern and polar reading to the conversation. He hears Ophiuchus as a bend in a river nudging you toward the circumpolar sky, Ursa Major and Minor, and the older stellar tradition that predates solar worship. Citing John Michell's book At the Center of the World, he describes European villages built as concentric rings around a tree, mound or standing stone that copied the pole star. He also presses the case that Ophiuchus is tied to Mercury and Hermes through the Caduceus, the divine androgyne and the phallus."}, {"title": "Twelve Around a Hidden Thirteenth", "body": "Mathisen credits Scott Onstott with pointing him to John Michell's Twelve Tribe Nations, which finds the same layout in Israel, Madagascar, Iceland, Ireland, Wales and among the Inca. Twelve are arranged north, south, east and west, and a thirteenth sits at the center where the connection to the divine lives. Garza links the pattern to the thirteenth card of the tarot, the hanged man's twelve branches and the twelve disciples with Christ as the thirteenth. Ophiuchus becomes the hub, the axle, the clutch between the engine of the divine and the wheels on the ground."}, {"title": "Etymology, Kush and the Snake Legged Gods", "body": "Chance Garton drives a long philological thread. The brazen serpent of Moses is nakash, and that kash is the kush in Ophiuchus, the same Kush who begat Nimrod. Bacchus comes from the Phoenician Bar-cus, son of Kush, and Krishna means swarthy or black just as Ham does. He even reads Abraxas as father, sun and Kush. Mathisen matches this with images, showing Zeus fighting the serpent legged Typhon, the anguiped Abraxas on Mithraic gems, the Apkalu of Nineveh with its handbag, and the Olmec feathered serpent at La Venta."}, {"title": "Myth as a Map of Buried Trauma", "body": "The heart of the episode is Mathisen's claim, laid out in Myth and Trauma and his newer Invoking the Ancient Gods in You, that these stories describe the higher self we suppress. He leans on Gabor Mate, Peter Levine and Richard Schwartz's internal family systems, reading Joseph thrown in the pit by twelve brothers and Inanna hung on a hook as pictures of a self that always returns. Garton adds that healing means seeing how trauma shaped behavior, finding the gap between stimulus and response, and refusing the Baudrillard style hyperreality people escape into."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Astrotheology author David Warner Mathisen returns to InnerVerse alongside fan favorite Mario Garza for a comprehensive overview of the symbolism in myth and religion that is contained within the enigmatic serpent-bearing constellation, Ophiuchus. Join us to learn of the vast array of wisdom characters derived from the mysterious asterism, and what they teach us about the gateway through which trauma programming is transcended, and the recovery of the higher self and divine spark.
